subject: Discovery recap + next steps — Redwood x AfternoonStar
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellie Summers <ellie@afternoonstar.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps — Redwood x AfternoonStar

Hi Ellie / Amit,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the candid conversation about AfternoonStar's content personalization roadmap. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps.

Summary of what we heard
- Current goal: reduce per-user recommendation latency while increasing freshness of personalized headlines; expect ~20M daily active users by Q4.
- Constraints: strict data residency requirements for EU users, and a short engineering runway (Q2 prioritization).
- KPIs: 95th percentile latency < 150ms for recommendation endpoint; target 30% reduction in per-request inference cost.

How Redwood maps to this
- Serving runtime: low-latency inference with continuous batching and KV-prefix caching to hit 95th pct latency targets.
- Deployment: we can run a Private VPC for EU traffic to satisfy residency + hosted API for US workloads.
- Cost controls: recommendations on quantization profiles and intelligent routing to save ~25–40% on token/compute costs.

Proposed next steps
1) Mutual action plan (attached) — scope, timeline, success metrics.
2) 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra lead to validate network/KMS constraints (suggested owners: Neha + Marcus; you can invite Amit).
3) Pilot: 2-week pilot on a sample traffic slice (we can scope once we align on infra).

Can you confirm whether this aligns with what you heard on your side? If yes, are you available for a technical deep-dive next week (options: Wed 2/18 10–11am PT or Thu 2/19 1–2pm PT)?

Attachment: AfternoonStar_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
